rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said.' Standard discourse-introducer in the Kephalaia, combined with ⲧⲟⲧⲉ 'then.'
Compound: ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix 'do/make') + ⲃⲁⲗ ('eye') + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('out, forth') = 'put-eye-forth, peer out.' Used here of the souls/light-particles peering out from the Living Soul-tree.
Lycopolitan adverbial 'in this manner, thus' — equivalent to Sahidic ⲛ̄ⲑⲉ. Used here in 'in the manner of fish' (line 14) and at line 13/18 (manner-comparative).
Lycopolitan contracted form of ⲥⲱⲧⲏⲣ (Greek σωτήρ). Title of Jesus introducing the dominical saying about the axe at the root of the tree.
Lycopolitan demonstrative + ⲛⲁⲩ 'hour, moment.' Standard time-marker 'until now / up to this moment.'
ⲛⲉϩⲧ likely a Lycopolitan verbal form of 'give, bear' (or ⲛⲁ-ϯ future). With ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ as object: 'bear fruit.'
Lycopolitan ⲧⲃⲧ = Sahidic ⲧⲏⲃⲧ 'fish.' Plural ⲍⲛ̄ⲧⲃⲧ 'fish.' Standard Manichaean simile for hidden/captured light-particles.
Possibly ⲧ-ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' or ⲧ-ϩⲱⲣⲃ̄ⲥ̄ 'covering, veil.' Confidence low.
Possibly ⲣ̄- + ⲁⲡⲱⲃⲥ̄ (Lyc. for ⲱⲃϣ̄ 'forget'). Context (archons after attempted resistance to the Living Spirit) fits 'were dazed/recoiled.' Tentative.
Possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲥⲱϩⲙ̄ 'rebuke, threaten' or ⲥⲉϩⲙ̄ 'plot.' With ⲟⲩⲃⲉ 'against,' fits hostile-stance verb. Tentative.
Abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲟⲩⲁ ('one') + ⲍⲏⲧ ('heart') = 'state of one-heartedness, single-mindedness.' Used of the unified manifestations of the Living Spirit.

Plural noun in series of multiple-manifestation modifiers (faces, multitudes, X, guises). Etymology unclear; possibly related to ⲃⲱⲕ 'go' = 'goings, modes of motion,' or to ⲃⲏⲕⲉ 'wages/things.' Tentative.
Compound: ϣ- (modal 'be able') + ⲛⲟⲩⲍⲙ̄ ('escape, be saved'). Lyc. spelling. Common Manichaean soteriological lexeme used here in negation: 'none could escape.'
Obscure compound — possibly Lyc. for 'from his hand/grasp' (cf. ⲥⲁ ⲣⲁⲧϥ̄ or related compound preposition). Translation tentative; confidence low.
